additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional Disorder is characterized by one or more fixed delusional beliefs lasting at least one month, without the broader disorganization, hallucinations, or negative symptoms typical of schizophrenia. Functioning may remain relatively intact outside the area touched by the belief, and the presentation is often organized and plausible enough that the condition becomes evident only when the belief persists despite clear contradictory evidence.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient.stressor: Roy was asked to lead a high-stakes scientific localization project with multiple subcontractors, new quality-control authority, and direct contact with a demanding international client, a step that felt tied to his hopes for senior management. In the early weeks he treated minor translation-memory inconsistencies as ordinary problems to solve, but over the next 11 months these concerns hardened into a fixed belief that specific people were intentionally manipulating the project record against him, even when audit trails and colleagues’ explanations contradicted it. He continued meeting deadlines and maintaining family routines, but the belief began to dominate project discussions and made routine collaboration tense enough that he contacted his company’s employee assistance program, initially asking for help managing work stress, and was referred for psychiatric evaluation.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: Outside the project issue, I still translate, manage my team’s workflow, pay bills, and keep up with my family routines. The only place things really go off track is when the file history or certain coworkers come up.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I haven’t lost my job or missed major deadlines, but project meetings have become tense because I keep pressing for the record to be corrected. A few colleagues now avoid looping me into routine discussions unless they have to.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about 11 months, since shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project.
